quotes.t: Treading along in this dreamlike, illusory realm,Without looking for the traces I may have left;A cuckoo's song beckons me to return home;Hearing this, I tilt my head to seeWho has told me to turn back;But do not ask me where I am going,As I travel in this limitless world,Where every step I take is my home.
quotes.c: As translated in The Zen Poetry of Dōgen: Verses from the Mountain of Eternal Peace (1997) by Steven Heine, p. 61

quotes.t: All the Buddhas, whether in this world or in other quarters, in the western heaven (India) or the eastern earth (China), equally held the Buddha-seal and altogether enjoyed the supreme style. They were fully devoted to this total sitting (shikantaza) and were totally installed in this unmoved state. Even though there are a thousand differences and a million nuances, they engaged devotedly in practicing zazen and realizing the Way.
quotes.c: A Universal Recommendation for True Zazen

quotes.t: As I study both the exoteric and the esoteric schools of Buddhism, they maintain that human beings are endowed with Dharma-nature by birth. If this is the case, why did the Buddhas of all ages - undoubtedly in possession of enlightenment - find it necessary to seek enlightenment and engage in spiritual practice?
quotes.c: As quoted in Eihei Dogen, Mystical Realist (2004) by Hee-jin Kim

quotes.t: Because monks come from the midst of purity, they consider as good and pure what does not arouse desire among other people.
Buddhas and Ancestors continuously maintain ocean mudra samadhi. While swimming in this samadhi, they expound, realize, practice.
But do not ask me where I am going, As I travel in this limitless world, Where every step I take is my home.
quotes.c: As translated in The Zen Poetry of Dōgen: Verses from the Mountain of Eternal Peace (1997) by Steven Heine, p. 61

quotes.t: Coming, going, the waterbirds don't leave a trace don't follow a path.
quotes.c: As quoted in The Enlightened Heart: An Anthology of Sacred Poetry (1989) by Stephen Mitchell, p. 50

quotes.t: Furthermore, form and substance are like dew on a blade of grass, and fleeting life is as a flash of lightning, instantly emptied and immediately lost.
quotes.c: A Universal Recommendation for True Zazen, (Note: This is an allusion to the final gāthā (verses) of the Diamond Sutra.)

quotes.t: If he cannot stop the mind that seeks after fame and profit, he will spend his life without finding peace.
In the great way of going beyond, no endeavor is complete without being one with myriad things. This is ocean mudra samadhi.
It is only due to a lack of heart for the Way and a lack of skill in handling their daily conduct that people become vainly tied to fame and gain.
quotes.c: Shōbōgenzō (1231-53), "Shobogenzo: The Treasure House of the Eye of the True Teaching" (2007) by Rev. Hubert Nearman, O.B.C. Chapter 29, p. 421

quotes.t: Just practice good, do good for others, without thinking of making yourself known so that you may gain reward. Really bring benefit to others, gaining nothing for yourself. This is the primary requisite for breaking free of attachments to the Self.
Just study Buddhism. Don't follow the sentiments of the world.
People who truly follow the Way would do well to conceal the fact that they are Buddhists.

Something you want badly enough can always be gained. No matter how fierce the enemy, how remote the beautiful lady, or how carefully guarded the treasure, there is always a means to the goal for the earnest seeker. The unseen help of the guardian gods of heaven and earth assure fulfillment.

Students of the Way must not study Buddhism for the sake of themselves. They must study Buddhism only for the sake of Buddhism. The key to this is to renounce both body and mind without holding anything back and to offer them to the great sea of Buddhism.
Students today should begrudge every moment of time. This dewlike life fades away; time speeds swiftly. In this short life of ours, avoid involvement in superfluous things and just study the Way.
Students, when you want to say something, think about it three times before you say it. Speak only if your words will benefit yourselves and others. Do not speak if it brings no benefit.

Therefore, you must stop comprehending the conduct of investigating words and chasing discourses. You must learn to step backward to turn your light around to reflect on yourself. Mind and body will naturally fall away and your original face will manifest itself. If you wish to attain suchness, devote yourself to suchness at once.
quotes.c: A Universal Recommendation for True Zazen

quotes.t: To study the Buddha way is to study oneself. To study oneself is to forget oneself. To forget oneself is to be enlightened by the myriad dharmas. To be enlightened by the myriad dharmas is to bring about the dropping away of body and mind of both oneself and others. The traces of enlightenment come to an end, and this traceless enlightenment is continued endlessly. When a person starts to search out the dharma, he separates himself far from the dharma. When the dharma has already been rightly transmitted in oneself, just then one is one's original self.
quotes.c: Shōbōgenzō (1231-53), Fascicle 1 (Genjokoan) of Shobogenzo, trans. Paul Jaffe (1996), in Yasutani, Flowers Fall (Boston: Shambhala), 101-107.

quotes.t: When other sects speak well of Zen, the first thing that they praise is its poverty.

Yet you must not cling to the words of the old sages either; they, too, may not be right. Even if you believe them, you should be alert so that, in the event that something superior comes along, you may follow that.
Zazen is the ultimate practice. This is indeed the True Self. The Buddhadharma is not to be sought outside of this.
Enlightenment is intimacy with all things.
Enlightenment is like the moon reflected on the water. The moon does not get wet, nor is the water torn. Although its light is wide and great, the moon is reflected even in a puddle an inch wide.
In the midst of activity, be quiet. In the midst of words, keep silence. In the midst of giving, be receiving.
The mind creates the world.
The mind that is attached to anything defiles the whole body.
The mind that is not disturbed by the passing of phenomena is the Way.
The self that is not the body and not the mind is called the true self.
The truth is not something that can be tasted by the tongue.
The truth of the universe is not something to be attained. It is something to be realized.
The way of the Buddha is to be free from all concepts of self and other.
The way of the Buddha is to be free from all systems of thought.
To know the world without ever going out of your door, you must go out of your door to know the world.
To practice is to confirm the self; to confirm the self is to forget the self.
To study Buddhism is to study the self. To study the self is to forget the self. To forget the self is to be enlightened by all things.
To study the Way is to study the self, to study the self is to forget the self, to forget the self is to be actualized by myriad things.
When all things are seen equally as the truth, one understands that one is nothing special.
When all things are seen equally as the truth, one understands the meaning of 'flowing with the world' and 'being one with the world'.
When you ride in a boat and watch the shore, you might assume that the shore is moving. But when you keep your eyes close to the boat, you can see that the boat moves.
When you walk, the wind blows; when you stop, you are still.
You should study not only the ancient sages but also the dust in your own room.
